## Course setup

- Parallel to the first-year **programming** course
- This course: biological questions → quantitative tools
- 14 weeks; each week has `slides.qmd`, `notebook.qmd`, `assignment.qmd` under `weeks/week-XX/`

### Biological arc

```text
Eco  →  Evo (deterministic → random)  →  Microbiome (ecology with randomness)
```

| Block | Weeks | Biology | Quantitative focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hook** | 1 | Human adaptation (Bajau / Andika) | Why cool biology needs quantitative tools |
| **Ecology** | 2–4 | Populations & interactions | Deterministic simulation (function → vector → loop) |
| **Evolution (deterministic)** | 5–7 | Allele-frequency change, selection | Recurrence equations; same coding engine |
| **Evolution (random)** | 8–10 | Drift; noisy allele-frequency paths | Stochastic simulation; matrices; uncertainty |
| **Microbiome** | 11–13 | Communities, diversity, environment | Ecology again — but high-dimensional & noisy |
| **Synthesis** | 14 | Microbiome project | Pull the arc together |

**Punchline of the semester:** you first learn deterministic ecological dynamics, then evolutionary change (smooth, then noisy), then return to ecology in a modern, data-rich, noisy form — **microbiomes**.

### Programming bridge

| Concept | Where |
|---|---|
| Function | next-state updates |
| Vector | ecological / genetic time series |
| Loop | many steps / generations |
| Plot | interpretation |
| Matrix | many stochastic runs; microbiome tables later |

## Week 1 — Hook: cool biology needs many tools

**Biology:** Bajau diving adaptation (Andika)  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-01/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-01/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-01/assignment.qmd)

- Personal story + photo hook
- Physiology → genetics → deep-history methods
- Papers: Ilardo et al. 2018 *Cell*; Ilardo et al. 2021 *Front. Physiol.*; Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014 *Nature*

## Ecology (Weeks 2–4)

Engine: biological rule → discrete update → `next_state()` → vectors → loop → plot

### Week 2 — From cool dynamics to code
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-02/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-02/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-02/assignment.qmd)

- **Bio opener integrated:** *Paramecium* alone vs with *Didinium* (Gause / Veilleux tradition)
- Data in `weeks/week-02/data/`
- Discrete LV → function / vector / loop; qualitative link back to the contrast

### Week 3 — Richer ecological models
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-03/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-03/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-03/assignment.qmd)

- Carrying capacity; optional extra species; parameter play

### Week 4 — Ecological data & your own model
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-04/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-04/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-04/assignment.qmd)

- Real time series; build a small ecological model

---

## Evolution — deterministic (Weeks 5–7)

Same engine; object = **allele frequency** \(p_t\).

### Week 5 — Allele frequencies as time series
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-05/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-05/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-05/assignment.qmd)

- Vectors for \(p_t\); selection recurrence \(p_{t+1}=f(p_t)\); one-generation function

### Week 6 — Selection regimes
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-06/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-06/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-06/assignment.qmd)

- Many generations; compare regimes; equilibria / trajectories

### Week 7 — Limits of deterministic evolution
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-07/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-07/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-07/assignment.qmd)

- Smooth \(p_t\) as average behavior; motivate randomness

---

## Evolution — random (Weeks 8–10)

### Week 8 — Why randomness in evolution?
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-08/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-08/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-08/assignment.qmd)

- Noisy paths; finite populations

### Week 9 — Wright–Fisher: one trajectory
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-09/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-09/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-09/assignment.qmd)

- One stochastic run vs deterministic expectation

### Week 10 — Many runs, matrices, uncertainty
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-10/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-10/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-10/assignment.qmd)

- Replicates in matrices; means / ribbons; drift vs selection (stretch)

---

## Microbiome — ecology with randomness (Weeks 11–13)

Return to ecological thinking, but now communities are **high-dimensional** and **noisy** (many taxa, compositional data, biological + technical variation).

### Week 11 — Communities as data
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-11/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-11/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-11/assignment.qmd)

- Abundance tables; what is a sample / taxon / count
- First plots; broad biological patterns

### Week 12 — Diversity & structure
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-12/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-12/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-12/assignment.qmd)

- Diversity summaries; compare groups
- Ecology concepts meet noisy multivariate data

### Week 13 — Environment & variation
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-13/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-13/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-13/assignment.qmd)

- Link metadata / gradients to community variation
- Uncertainty and interpretation (not overclaiming)

---

## Week 14 — Project: pull the arc together

**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-14/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-14/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-14/assignment.qmd)

- Default: microbiome exploratory project
- Allowed: Eco or Evo question using tools from earlier blocks
- Story + plots + careful claims
